This is Mak Yong. Pre-Islamic court and folk tradition.
on_screen: Title card: Mak Yong · Malaysia · Pre-Islamic court and folk tradition

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Mak yong originated in the Pattani Kingdom and spread to Kelantan and Kedah over 200 years ago.
Passed down orally among villagers, it is estimated to be at least 800 years old.
It was patronized by the Kelantan Sultanate until the 1920s.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Mak yong served as entertainment, harvest thanksgiving, and healing rituals (such as mak yong mak puteri involving trance-dancing and spirit possession).
It acts as a mystical conduit to the spirit world and honors teachers and graduates.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Performances open with an offering (semah kampung) followed by dancing, acting, and improvised dialogues across three-hour shows over several nights.
Most roles are performed by women, featuring the Pak Yong (king), a queen, palace girls, and male jesters.
A group called Jong Dongdang performs songs and dances between chapters.
on_screen: Formation: performed on a temporary open stage built of wood and palm leaves
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The orchestra features the rebab (a three-stringed spiked lute), gendang (double-headed barrel drums), a pair of gongs (tetawak), serunai (flute), keduk drums, and kesi (small cymbals).
Its singing and musical repertoire are distinct and unique to the region.
Listen for the rebab, gendang, gongs, serunai.
Led by the three-stringed spiked lute (rebab), accompanied by double-headed barrel drums (gendang) and hanging knobbed gongs, creating a distinct traditional Malay theatrical sound.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performances traditionally use elaborate costumes where the lead Pak Yong dresses like a king.
In villages, performances are held on temporary open stages built of wood and palm leaves, with the audience sitting on three sides and the orchestra on the fourth.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The late Cik Ning was a leading mak yong performer in the 1980s.
Long Abdul Ghaffar supported the art in 1923 by building Kampung Temenggung on palace grounds, an effort later continued by Khatijah Awang's Seri Temenggong group.

Variations include Makyong United (Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat), Makyong Kelantan, Makyong Kedah, Makyong Mar (Perlis and Satun), Makyong Riau (Indonesia), Field Makyong (Medan, Indonesia), and Makyong Kalimantan (Indonesia).
Stories are derived from Kelantan or Patani mythology, including tales like 'Anak Raja Gondang' originating from Buddhist Jataka tales.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Mak yong contains deep animist and pre-Islamic spiritual elements, historically involving offerings to spirits (semah kampung), spirit possession, and healing rituals (main puteri), which led to past religious bans.
